Vivek,

Appreciate you taking this. We received the renewal proposal yesterday and the list price + forthcoming platform change has materially shifted our forecast. On top of that, November included two incidents that impacted our data pipeline for ~6 hours total. Our finance team is flagging the renewal and asking us to evaluate alternatives.

- Immediate credit for the November outage (we estimate ~$12k in impact).
- Pause/roll back the planned price increase for year one of the renewal.
- A firm SLA add-on (99.9% + defined credits) or a trial of the new infra at no additional cost for 90 days.

We want to stay with Redwood — the product fits — but we need these items addressed before our procurement sign-off. Can we get a proposal that addresses these points today? We have a call with finance on Thursday.

Adding customer health context and a proposed concession structure.

Customer health: Fathom has been a steady mid-market account for 3 years (current ARR ~$180k). Product usage has grown 40% Y/Y but procurement cycles are tight — finance wants predictable spend for 2027. The Nov incidents appear tied to a downstream connector; they did have retries but they surfaced errors to analysts during a key reporting weekend.

Proposed retention package (tiered options):
A) Standard concession (no exec): 15% discount year one + 1 month of service credit (applied as invoice credit). SLA unchanged.
B) Manager-approved (requires sales lead signoff): 25% discount year one + 1 month service credit + priority remediation support for 90 days.
C) Executive-approved (ask here): 30% discount year one + 2 months service credit + SLA addendum (99.9% with explicit credit formula) OR 90-day infra upgrade trial + assignment of an implementation engineer for one quarter.

Rationale for C: we keep revenue, reduce churn risk, and signal we own the incident. Net present value favors keeping the account vs churn probability.

Attachments: fathom-proposal-v3.pdf (proposal with pricing scenarios).

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Quick finance/approval note — numbers and ask.

Deal snapshot:
- Current ARR: $180,000
- Proposed renewal term: 12 months (customer asks to avoid multi-year lock)
- Requested concession level (option C): ~30% off year one = ~$45k discount plus 2 months credit (~$30k) and SLA addendum
- Total first-year concession ~ $75k (~42% of first-year TCV on paper, less over lifetime)

Approval boundary: anything that implies >30% effective concession or credits >$50k requires VP/Sales + Finance signoff. Option C sits right at/near that boundary depending on how credits are applied. I recommend the following executive authorization language so we can move quickly:
- Authorize up to 30% off year-one list price AND up to $35k in invoice credits OR approval to offer the 90-day infra trial in lieu of monetary credits.
- Legal to prepare a contract addendum restricting the concession to a 12-month reset (no stacking of future credits) and a monitored MOP.

If we get OK by EOD tomorrow I will finalize the commercial amendment and aim for signature by Friday.

Lauren Bishop
Sales Lead, Mid-Market | Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:20:00 -08:00

Legal quick take and required clauses.

We can support the exec-authorized concession with the following guardrails:
- Contract addendum with explicit credit calculation: tie credits to incident window and documented impact (attachment: mop-addendum-draft.docx).
- One-time term reset to 12 months; add non-renewal penalty if customer terminates within 90 days (to protect revenue).
- SLA addendum: 99.9% with clearly defined measurement windows and cap on cumulative credits (e.g., credits capped at 3 months invoice over 12 months).
- Non-standard commercial approval: require Finance to sign off on revenue recognition impact (I will loop Finance once exec direction is confirmed).

Suggested redline language is in the attached draft. I recommend approving the option that includes the 90-day infra trial as an alternative to the full monetary credit — operationally easier and preserves cash.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
